intent: One option of a DropdownMenuRadioGroup, identified by a value unique within that group and showing a check while selected.
typical_uses: One entry of a sort order or a view mode chosen from a menu

dont_use_when.situation: A setting switched on and off on its own
An action that runs when chosen and selects nothing

invariants.text: Rendering the item outside a DropdownMenuRadioGroup throws; the primitive reads the selected value from the group's context.
Activating the item selects it and leaves the menu open, unless `closeOnClick` is true.
A check glyph, hidden from assistive technology, is rendered at the row's inline end only while the item is checked; the row reserves padding on its right side for it.
With `indicatorSide="start"` the glyph and its reserved padding move to the row's inline start and a checked row is also filled with the secondary color.
A `disabled` row stays in arrow-key navigation and can take focus, but pressing it or pressing Enter on it does nothing.

dropdown-menu.module.css sizes every descendant `svg` of the row to the small icon size and keeps it from shrinking or taking pointer events, so a leading icon passed in children needs no size of its own.

anti_patterns.dont: Reuse the same `value` for two items in one group
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give every item a unique `value` within its group; items sharing the group's value show as checked together and cannot be told apart

a11y.by: the primitive's Menu.RadioItem renders role="menuitemradio" with aria-checked; dropdown-menu.test.tsx asserts the item is found by the menuitemradio role and name and that clicking it reports its value through the group's onValueChange

value.states: value is the item's own value, of any type the caller chooses, required and compared against the group's value
value.because: The primitive declares `value: any` with no `?`, so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds, only that it must be present.

onClick.states: onClick is a callback called with the click event when the item is activated by pointer or keyboard
onClick.because: A React event handler - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the radio item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the radio item's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (checked, disabled, highlighted). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dropdown-menu.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside DropdownMenuRadioItem with a fixed check icon; only its side is exposed, as `indicatorSide`.

good.title: Options with the check on the leading edge
good.code:
<DropdownMenuRadioGroup value={sort} onValueChange={setSort}>
  <DropdownMenuRadioItem indicatorSide="start" value="name">Name</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
  <DropdownMenuRadioItem indicatorSide="start" value="date">Date</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
</DropdownMenuRadioGroup>

bad.title: A radio item placed straight in the popup
bad.why: There is no group to hold the selection, so the primitive throws; wrap the items in a DropdownMenuRadioGroup.

onClick.description: TS: ((event: BaseUIEvent<MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement, MouseEvent>>) => void) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. onClick is a callback called with the click event when the item is activated by pointer or keyboard. A React event handler - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, MenuRadioItemState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the radio item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: MenuRadioItemState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the radio item's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (checked, disabled, highlighted). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dropdown-menu.module.css, not through this.

value.description: TS: any. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. value is the item's own value, of any type the caller chooses, required and compared against the group's value. The primitive declares `value: any` with no `?`, so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds, only that it must be present.
